findings.before: afterEach calls initializeTools; its once-only lifecycle cannot restore registered overrides; 55 failures in subsequent resolution/doctrine/scope tests
findings.after: Fixture snapshots registered definitions and restores them in afterEach. A fresh subprocess deliberately fails with temporary overrides, then successfully executes the production tool in the next test. Original production restrictions and assertions retained.

findings.before: Detached async descendant successfully creates a Module after its index callback has returned
findings.after: Callback-scoped active authority is revoked in finally, files are copied, and persistence rechecks activity after admission awaits. Regression rejects the mutation and confirms no Module was persisted.

findings.before: Three CAS retry loops for admit, renew and release
findings.after: One private canonical admission-row update loop; no generalized lock framework. Expired leases are pruned. Renewal rejects invalid durations and cannot revive abandoned owners.

review.admission: One canonical Artifact and one conditional CAS owner. No SQL transaction across model work. Fresh-process exclusion, restart recovery, stale-owner renewal/refusal and idempotent release pass.
review.scope: One in-progress scope on canonical Ticket metadata; independently accepted VERIFY remains authoritative current proof. Restart retains pending scope after failed completion; successful completion clears it atomically. No parallel tracker or journal.
review.completion: Conditional public batch includes admission assertion, Ticket/claim revision, current proof replacement and verifies link. Injected SQL failure/restart tests pass; source validation remains resolver/change-engine responsibility, not a SQLite filesystem transaction.
review.limits: Trusted host owns indexing callback access. Truly independent OS processes remain outside managed tool permission enforcement. This narrow review is not the full Gate 5 whole-method release audit.
